instructions: Rinse the 2 cups of rice in a strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and keep the lid on until you serve.
Meanwhile, slice the thick Chinese broccoli stalks on a diagonal into 1-inch pieces. Cut the leaves into large pieces. Keep the stalks and leaves in separate piles.
In a small bowl, stir together the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and 1/4 cup water until the sugar dissolves. Mince the garlic cloves.
Slice the pork thinly, about 1/4 inch thick, and pat it dry. Sprinkle the pinch of salt over it.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat for 2 minutes, then add 1 tbsp of the oil.

Add half the pork in a single layer. Leave it alone for 1 minute, then stir for 1 minute, until browned with no pink left. Transfer it to a plate and cook the rest the same way, adding 1 tbsp of the oil.
You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest slice: it's done when there's no pink left.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil and the stalks. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, until they turn bright green.
Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds, until you can smell it. Add the leaves and stir for 30 seconds, until they wilt.
Return the pork and add the sauce. Toss for 1 minute, until the sauce is thick enough to coat everything and the pan is almost dry. Take it off the heat.
Slice the chili thinly and put it in a small bowl. Serve with the rice and the chili at the table.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Thai Cookbook's version, the best rated by far, is a quick stir-fry of garlic, sliced pork, oyster sauce, a little light soy sauce and sugar, with the Chinese broccoli added last for about 30 seconds. Only that one page was readable; the other pad kana pages found were the crispy pork belly dish or blocked, so no second version could be compared. This version scales the sauce for four, adds a splash of water so there is a little sauce for the rice, and moves the chili to the table.
